Title: Does Drawing Out the Beast cancels passive effects from equipment cards?

Messages.Author: Coyote
Messages.Body:
Does the "cannot use equipment" from "Drawing Out the Beast" cancels passive effects like having [SER] from a "The Book of Going Forth by Night" or only effects that require the player to actively use them?

Drawing Out the Beast

Name: Drawing Out the Beast
[Jyhad:C, VTES:C, SW:PT, FN:PR, CE:C, Anarchs:PG2, BH:PN3, Third:PTz3/SKTz2]
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Animalism
Only usable before range is determined on the first round. Frenzy.
[ani] During this combat, opposing vampire gets +1 strength, but he or she cannot use maneuvers to maneuver to long range, cannot use presses to end combat and cannot use equipment. A vampire may play only one Drawing Out the Beast each combat.
[ANI] As above, and the opposing vampire takes 1 unpreventable damage during the press step each round.
Artist: Bryon Wackwitz

The Book of Going Forth by Night

Name: The Book of Going Forth by Night
[KMW:PB, POD:DTC]
Cardtype: Equipment
Cost: 1 pool
Unique.
This vampire gets superior Serpentis [SER]. If an ally opposing this vampire in combat would be burned, instead steal and lock the ally; if the ally has lost their last life, they gain 1 life.
Artist: Steve Eidson

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Coyote wrote:
> Does the "cannot use equipment" from "Drawing Out the Beast" cancels passive effects like having [SER] from a "The Book of Going Forth by Night" or only effects that require the player to actively use them?
>
The former.

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: inm8
Messages.Body:
Not that it is needed, previous  ruling aligned with the above formulated a bit clearer.

> LSJ wrote:
> > 1. Drawing out the Beast prohibits the opposing vampire from using
> > equipment.
> >
> > 2. Some "effects" of equipment can be described as an actual "event",
> > "action" or "individual use" (such as using a flamethrower as a strike
> > to deal aggravated damage). Other times, equipment might give a minion
> > a certain "passive" or "aura" effect (borrowing terminology from WC3)
> > that is considered always effective without an actual declaration of
> > use (such as the Eye of Hazimel's granting of extra disciplines).
> If it applies to the minion, and is not a restriction (cannot
> hunt), then it is "using" it.
>
